reason: *h₂eǵ- + *gʷṓws: RV 2.12.3 gā́ udā́jat and 8.14.8 úd gā́ ājat (checked) = Lat. boves abigere (Livy 1.7.4, not local; cf. abigeus 'cattle thief'). Same thematic present. Builder misses Lat. bōs and marks the object interpolated. Vergil Aen. 8.203-205 should probably go: from memory (not local), agebat governs tauros there and boves is the subject of tenebant. OIr táin bó is root-level only.

*gʷʰn̥tó- + middle *ḱey-: RV 10.108.4 hatā́ … śayadhve, Il. 24.757-758 πρόσφατος … κεῖσαι, Yt. 10.80 sōire … jata (all checked). The builder doesn't credit -φατος or jata-. Same formula and the same Greek and Avestan loci as dragon-006 and death-004: one parallel for the eval split.

Fails the head rule. No clause head is shared: 'slay' is Vedic only, 'drive' is Latin only (Hes. Th. 287-291, checked in glaux, has ἐξενάριξε … ἤλασεν), and 'head' is not cognate. Only 'three' and 'cow' are shared, both high-frequency. 1 verified token of 10. A myth-level parallel, not shared wording. Hesiod is local, contrary to the note.
'Cattle and horses' (Il. 1.154, RV 10.108.7, both checked) is a generic wealth pair (P5). The verb, 'my' and the negation are Greek only.

Honest root-level line. The verb is shared only by root (Ved. ajati against Gk ἀγέλη, a noun; the Greek verb is ἐλαύνω), and gʰóstis stands in for non-cognate arí-. RV 1.33.3 and Il. 11.677-678 checked.

Watkins' *peh₂- wiHro- peku- (ch. 17, checked in watkins/). Umbr. ueiro pequo (Tab. Ig. VIa 30, checked in Buck 1904) = Av. pasuuā̊ vīraiiā̊ (Yt. 13.10 = YtFra2.10e, checked). The merism is sound. But the interpolated imperative ph₂dʰí is contradicted by every daughter that attests the stem (Ved. pāhí, Av. pāiδi; *ph₂-dʰí would give Ved. *pidhí). Fix the form or cut the line to the NP, and it is sound. Builder can't match Umbrian, so share = 0.

Vocative title *diwés dʰugh₂ter: RV 1.48.1 duhitar divaḥ and Il. 5.348 Διὸς θύγατερ (both checked). The verb and 'Dawn' are honestly interpolated; Od. 9.151 adds only Ἠώς. Same title as sky-014, with Rhesa no. 78 cited in both: group them for eval.

Secure share 0. 'Shine' is Greek only (φάνη), 'born' is root-level (jā́yamāna-, a -ye- present, against the compound ἠριγένεια), and the reduplicated participle ǵíǵn̥h₁omh₁neh₂es is in neither branch. Only the Dawn word is shared. After the round-2 cuts nothing is left that is a shared phrase.

West ch. 5 pairs φάε … Ἠώς (Od. 14.502) with Ved. bhā of Uṣas (RV 3.61.2 ví bhāhi), both checked. But the Greek is a 3sg past, the line is an imperative, and the root-imperative bʰh₂dʰí is contradicted by Ved. bhāhí (full grade).

Middle voice is now correct (yukṣvá, ζεύγνυσθ', RV 1.92.15 and Od. 23.244-246 checked). Still: different stems (s-aorist against -νυ- present), and the Greek is a negated infinitive. Yoking horses is generic; only Dawn as the agent makes it specific.

*bʰer- + Dawn is shared (RV 10.35.5 jyótir bhárantīr uṣásaḥ, Il. 11.1-2 φόως φέροι, both checked; also Od. 23.245). The object is not cognate (jyótis- against φάος), and the interpolated bʰéh₂os is not φάος's formation (*φάϝος).

Contradiction. In Hes. Th. 371-374 (checked in glaux, though the note says not local) Theia bears Helios, Selene and Eos, so Dawn is the Sun's sister, not his mother. 'The Dawns bore the Sun' is a Vedic-only proposition (RV 7.78.3, checked). The formations also differ: reduplicated aorist against γείνατο.

West ch. 5 notes the cognate epithet (RV 3.2.7 svàr mahát, Hes. Th. 19 Ἠέλιον μέγαν, both checked), but 'great' + 'sun' is generic. Both branches have it attributive; the line makes it predicative with an interpolated copula.

spáś- against σκοπός is root-level, as the note says (RV 4.13.3 and Hymn. Dem. 62, both checked; the Hymn is local in glaux). The builder's 'exact' for Greek is a false positive: a 3-letter prefix match on σκώψ.

Secure share 0. 'Goes up' is Vedic only (ἀνόρουσε is another verb). márteṣu is governed by páśyan ('looking at … among mortals'), not 'for mortals'. Ved. márta- (full grade) is not exactly βροτός (*mr̥tó-). What's left is the sun rising for people, a commonplace.
'The sun shines' is the commonest possible collocation (P5). There is no scholarly claim of inheritance, and φαείνω is a derived present against Ved. bhā́ti. RV 10.121.6 and Od. 12.385 checked.

Only the NP 'wheel of the Sun' is shared (cakrám sū́ryasya = κύκλος ἀελίοιο). 'Horse' is Greek only and 'draw' Vedic only. West doubts the image is PIE. Eur. El. 464-466 is local in glaux (checked), contrary to the note. The NP overlaps dawn-014.

'Eye of Sky' rests on RV 1.72.10 divó … akṣī́ (dual, sun and moon; checked) and Macrobius' late report. The 'eye' words are different formations (ákṣ-/ákṣi- against the diminutive oculus). Greek is properly support only.

A real West parallel ('to live is to see the sun', West ch. 2). 'Live' is root-level and 'see' is Vedic only. The optative mood comes from RV 10.37.7, a support ref, so P2 leaks into the output. All loci checked.

The note is wrong in the cautious direction. vedaweb has ájma- m., a thematic noun (mahó ájmasya, RV 4.53.4, checked), the same *-mo- formation as ὄγμος (Hymn. Hom. 32.11, checked in glaux). So the NP equation holds at formation level. But 'great' + 'course' is a natural pairing, West's 'exact equivalent' claim could not be found in the local text, the verb and the locative are interpolated, and LOC méǵh₂i has an unexpected full-grade root.

Only one formation-level noun is shared (támas : tenebrae). The verbs differ (a causative gamaya against uiso), and with 'lower' now interpolated, West's NP formula ('lower darkness') is gone. RV 10.152.4 is a curse sending an enemy below; Lucr. 1.115 is about the soul's fate (both checked). Darkness as the place of the dead is near-universal.

3pl 'the slain lie': Yt. 10.80 sōire … jata and RV 1.133.1 hatā́ḥ … áśeran (both checked), with Il. 24.757-758. The 3pl middle -n̥tor is defensible (Homeric κέαται; Indo-Iranian has the r-ending, which the note flags). Duplicates the formula of cattle-002 and dragon-006 (same Greek and Avestan loci).

Secure share 0, and every shared item is root-level: κοιμάω (a derivative of *ḱey-), Ved. svap- (a verb) against ὕπνος (a noun). The Greek has a cognate accusative and the locative is interpolated. 'Death as sleep' here is thematic. RV 1.121.11 and Il. 11.241 checked.

A single lexeme (νέκυς; OIr éc means 'death', not 'the dead') with non-cognate verbs. 'Go to the dead' is a near-universal idiom. The OIr is an idiom quoted from West, not a locus. Il. 15.251-252 checked.

A real invocation parallel (RV 10.61.4, checked; Alcaeus fr. 34, not local). The head 'son' is renewed in both branches and interpolated. In RV 10.61.4 me is possessive (me yajñám, me ánnam: 'my sacrifice', 'my food'), not 'come to me', so the moy parallel is weaker than the note says. Only diwés is secure.

'Daughter of the Sun' is shared (RV 1.117.13, checked; Lith. Sáulės dukrýtė, not local), though Sáulė against sū́rya- is root-level. The clause is Vedic only. Form problems: 'of you two' comes out as plural wos (the plan has DU), and avr̥ṇīta is the imperfect of a nasal present, not a root aorist.

Stitched from RV 10.85.14 and 1.117.12-13 (two hymns, three stanzas; checked). Its only secure NP is the one twins-002 already uses (same RV 1.117.13, same dainos). The Vedic áyātam is 2du; the line has 3du. 6 tokens, 1 verified.

The formula is real (Watkins *h₁ōḱéwes h₁éḱwōs; Il. 5.275 ὠκέας ἵππους, checked). But in RV 8.5.7 (checked) āśúbhiḥ goes with śyenébhiḥ in pāda b and áśvebhiḥ stands in pāda c: use RV 1.117.9 or 7.71.5 āśúm áśvam, also of the Aśvins. The engine's INS.PL HHḱéwbʰis (zero-grade root, full-grade suffix) is contradicted by Ved. āśúbhiḥ and Gk ὠκ-.

Bahuvrihi *h₁su-h₁éḱwo- of the Twins in both branches: sváśvā … yātam (RV 7.69.3, checked) = εὔιπποι Τυνδαρίδαι (Pind. Ol. 3.39, checked in glaux, contrary to the note; West ch. 4 makes the comparison). The verb is honestly interpolated. The builder can't credit compounds (share 0).

Pastiche. 'Young' (yúvānā, RV 1.117.14) and 'sons of Sky' (1.117.12) come from different stanzas. The Greek gives only Διός (Hymn 33.1, checked in glaux), and the Latin iuuenes is Cicero's prose. h₂yéwHonh₁ has a full-grade root against Ved. yúvan- and Lat. iuu- (zero grade).

Only 'ship' is shared, a high-frequency noun; the verb and the object are Vedic only. The vocative 'Sons of Sky' in the output comes from a support ref (RV 1.117.12): P2 leaks into the PIE. The Alcaeus wording is unverified (West prints a translation). Hymn. Hom. 33.8 νηῶν (local) would have been the checkable Greek.

Watkins' Basic Formula: past of *gʷʰen- in RV 1.32.1, Y. 9.8 and KBo 12.84 (Indo-Iranian checked). Hittite gives only the verb, so the serpent is one-branch, as Watkins' own formula has it. The Greek is now support (Pyth. 4.249 has κτεῖνε, checked).

The relative + *gʷʰen- appears in three traditions (Y. 9.8, RV 2.12.11, Od. 5.128, all checked), and κατέπεφνε is *gʷʰen-, which the builder misses. But the Greek is a reduplicated aorist (root-level), and 'Zeus who slew him (Iasion)' is a generic relative clause, not a hero defined by his monster-slaying. The serpent is Indo-Iranian only.

*h₁ógʷʰis … ḱéytor (RV 1.32.5, checked) with *gʷʰn̥tó- + *ḱey- (Yt. 10.80 jata sōire, Il. 24.757-758 πρόσφατος κεῖσαι). The serpent is Vedic only and honestly interpolated. Same formula as cattle-002 and death-004.

Better Vedic locus: RV 4.19.3 suṣupāṇám āśáyānam áhim (checked) beside Beowulf 2746-2747 ligeð, swefeð (checked). But only *swep- is shared, at root level, and 'lie' is two different roots (*legʰ- against *ḱey-). Secure share 0.

Wrong form in the only secure token. The INS.SG sh₂inéh₁ drops the m of *sh₂i-mn- (the engine's weak stem is sh₂in-: GEN sh₂inés), against Hitt. išḫimanta and OE sīmon. Also, the interpolated verb sinéh₂- is taken from RV 7.84.2, a support ref ('without ropes'). The parallel itself (KUB 17.5 i 15′ and Genesis 766, both checked) is fine: regenerate after fixing the n-stem.

Watkins ch. 43 is real (Grípisspá 11, Beowulf 587, RV 1.4.8, all checked). The predicate noun matches at formation level, but 'become' is renewed, and 'serpent' is interpolated where both texts have other words. The interpolated GEN h₁égʷʰis is contradicted by Ved. áheḥ. In Grípisspá 11 'bane' governs Regin ok Fáfni; orm goes with vega.

Watkins pp. 327-328 (checked) explicitly equates RV 8.84.9 nákir yáṃ ghnánti hánti yáḥ (checked) with OIr gonait 7 ní genaiter (TBDD 783, not local) as 'the slayer not slain'. *gʷʰen- in both clauses in both branches. Voice follows the Vedic. The builder can't match OIr gonaid, so share = 0: fix the flags.
Clause 1 *gʷʰen- + serpent is fine (KUB 17.5 i 18′, RV 6.20.2, both checked). Clause 2 'the gods were with him' is Hittite only (logographic DINGIRMEŠ, katti=šši). 1 verified token of 6.

dʰedʰh₁dʰí is now correct. But the Greek is stitched from two texts, both unverifiable (Krisa for ἄφθιτον, Timocreon PMG 728 for τίθει; glaux has only Timocreon's epigram). The builder never matches ákṣita- = ἄφθιτος. Same RV 1.9.7 as fame-001, fame-004 and poetics-012.
The frame (ἔχοι 'may he have') is Greek only and rests on the unverifiable Krisa inscription. The NP is the one already in fame-001, fame-002 and poetics-012 (same RV 1.9.7).
máhi śrávaḥ = μέγα κλέος (RV 1.79.4, 1.43.7, Od. 2.125, Il. 6.446, all checked), with the beneficiary dative in both. The verb is now the correct present dʰedʰh₁dʰí, honestly interpolated.
Only ḱléwos is secure. 'Wide' is the compound member urugāyá- against κλέος εὐρύ (root-level), and the verb is Vedic only. RV 6.65.6, Od. 3.83 and 1.344 checked.

The plural 'fames' with a genitive of the doer is shared (Il. 9.524, Od. 8.73, RV 8.99.2 táva śrávāṃsi, all checked). But the distinctive 'of men' is Greek only (West: narā́m śrávāṃsi 'cannot be documented'), and 'heard' is interpolated (Greek πεύθομαι).

Head *h₂is-sḱé- is exact (Ved. ichámāna-, RV 1.126.1 and 10.102.4, checked; OCS/ORuss. iskati, which the builder misses). The object is only root-level in Slavic (slava). The second branch is the late, contested Slovo (not local).

*h₁wésu ḱléwos (Y. 62.6c vaŋhāuca srauuahi, checked; OIr fó chlú, not local). The Avestan has a locative after zazəbuiiē, and the line an accusative. The frame is Avestan only. Same NP and the same OIr ref as poetics-013.
ὄνομα κλυτόν against śrútyaṃ nā́ma: śrútya- is another derivative (root-level), and 'bear' is Vedic only (bíbhrat, a participle). RV 5.30.5, Od. 9.364 and 19.183 checked.

On the reading the note itself adopts, RV 8.46.14 (checked) has no 'famous name': nā́ma is adverbial and śrútyam goes with índram. So only 'name' is shared, in passages with no common phrase. Also shares Od. 19.183 with fame-011.

Compound equation *h₁su-ḱléwes- (Ved. suśrávas- = Gk εὐκλεής, West ch. 10, checked). Both parallel loci checked: RV 1.91.21 and 1.49.2 suśrávasam, Od. 21.331 ἐϋκλεῖας predicated with ἔμμεναι. The nom. -ēs and the Vedic accent are defensible; the copula is honestly interpolated. A one-word formula; the builder can't credit compounds (share 0).

Heteroclitic polyptoton 'blood with blood': AVP 4.15.3 asṛk te asnā rohatu (DCS checked; the AVŚ correction is right) and KUB 55.20+ Vs. I 17-18 ešḫar=kan ešḫani ḫandan (TLH checked). The verb is honestly interpolated. The builder has no Hittite key, so share = 0.

The marrow clause is a one-branch proposition: no second branch has marrow-to-marrow, OHG is support only, and the marrow word is root-level. The second clause is healing-001 word for word, so it leaks a duplicate. The verb 'set' is stitched from AVŚ 4.12.5d (checked).

Watkins' reconstruction by contiguity, not an attested parallel. AVŚ 12.5 majjānam asya nirjahi (DCS checked). OHG and OIr each give one word, from texts that aren't local. Marrow is root-level. OIr gono is *gʷʰen-, which the builder misses.

Common words, a thematic parallel (the note says so itself). *steh₂- is root-level: Ved. práti tiṣṭha (AVŚ 4.12.6, DCS checked), an intransitive present, against Pindar's transitive ἔστασεν ὀρθούς (Pyth. 3.53, checked in glaux). The ūrdhvá-/ὀρθός equation is disputed. Share 0.

'Bone with bone': AVP 4.15.2 asthnāsthy api rohatu (DCS checked) and KUB 55.20+ Vs. I 16 ḫaštai=kan ḫaštai ḫandan (TLH checked); Hitt. ḫaštai- is a true cognate of *h₃ésth₁. The verb is honestly interpolated. The INS h₃sth₁éh₁ lacks the Vedic n (asthnā́), but that n is the Indic i/n-stem pattern (ákṣi/akṣṇ-, dádhi/dadhn-), and Hitt. ḫaštai- has its own -i- extension. Handbooks give the oblique *h₃sth₁- without n, so this is not counted as a contradicted form. The builder has no Hittite key.

The NP 'carpenters of words' stands in no cited text. In Pyth. 3.112-113 (checked in glaux, contrary to the note) ἐπέων depends on ἐξ and τέκτονες is the subject of ἅρμοσαν; Nem. 3.4 has τέκτονες κώμων. The Vedic has a different agent noun in a simile (táṣṭeva, RV 3.38.1, 1.61.4), and the Avestan a compound (N. 5.2). The *wékʷos/*tetḱ- collocation belongs to poetics-001.

Benfey's δῶτορ ἑάων = dātā́ vásūnām (Od. 8.335, RV 8.51.5, both checked), with Y. 16.1 correctly demoted to support. The Greek -τωρ supports the root-accented déh₃tor and the Vedic the oxytone, which the note acknowledges. The verb is interpolated. Shares RV 8.51.5 with poetics-007.

Only 'horse' is shared. 'Song' (gír- against dúan) and 'give' (dā- against do-beir) are not cognate. Watkins compares the institution (horses as the poet's fee), not wording. The Irish text isn't local. RV 6.63.10 checked.
The secure NP is the same as fame-005's and uses the same Od. 2.125-126. Its own content, 'make' (kṛdhi against ποιεῖτ'), is a semantic frame with non-cognate verbs. RV 5.18.5 checked.

*misdʰó- is a specific technical term (mīždəm, Y. 44.18, checked; μισθόν, Pyth. 1.75-77, checked in glaux) in a 'win the reward' frame. The verbs are not cognate (han- against ἀρέομαι), and 'how' is Avestan only.

Root-aorist imperative *ḱludʰí exact (κλῦθι, śrudhí; Il. 1.37, RV 1.25.19, both checked), plus a 1sg enclitic. Homer always has the genitive κλῦθί μευ (8 times in the treebank, never μοι), so *moy follows Ved. me (gen./dat.) and Greek has renewed the genitive enclitic. The builder marks it root-level, which is an undercount. Minor: in RV 1.25.19 me goes with hávam ('my call').

The core *dyéw ph₂ter is sound in three branches (RV 6.51.5, Il. 3.276, Cato Agr. 134.3 Iupiter, all checked). But the Earth half still has the engine's pl̥th₂éwih₂ (Greek-type -ew-ih₂, and the VOC keeps -ih₂), contradicted by Ved. pṛthivī́/pŕ̥thivi: round-1 P6 is not fixed. The OE 'Folde … mōdor' is not in the local Grein.

Only the kin terms are shared beyond Vedic. Lucretius' pater aether / mater terrai (1.250-251, checked) is a Greek-influenced topos, and Æcerbot is not local. The form pl̥th₂éwih₂ is still wrong. 9 tokens, 2 verified.

mahé pitré divé (RV 1.71.5, checked; RV 3.54.2 mahé divé) = Ζεῦ πάτερ … μέγιστε (Il. 3.276, checked). The cases follow the Vedic and the forms are right (m̥ǵh₂éy fits Ved. mahé). Unlike fame-006, whose secure core is one word, the core here is already the two-word *dyéw ph₂ter formula, plus 'great'. Shares Il. 3.276 with sky-001: one eval group. Note: Greek 'great' is the superlative here and the λ-stem in Il. 2.134, so the builder's 'exact' is generous.

Only the genitive 'of Sky' is shared. The heads differ (ὄμβρος against vr̥ṣṭí-), and the note itself says the line fails the head rule. A semantic parallel ('Sky's rain') with one cognate modifier. Il. 5.91, RV 5.83.6 and 5.63.4 checked.

Root-level throughout (sádman- against the compound -εδής). The output head sédos comes from a support ref (Hes. Th. 117), so P2 leaks, and 'earth' and 'for the gods' are interpolated. The builder's 'exact' for 'broad' is a prefix match on a compound. Simonides isn't local.
Only diwés is shared (Hymn 33.1 Διὸς κούρους, checked in glaux; RV 1.182.1, checked). Head and predicate are interpolated, and it overlaps twins-001 and twins-006 (same Hymn 33.1).

Zero verified tokens. Among the parallel refs, dyēws is Vedic only, 'mother' is OE only (Æcerbot, not local), the verb is interpolated, and the Earth name is root-level. A pastiche of a ploughman's prayer. Hes. Op. 465 and Cato 134.2 checked.

*diwés dʰugh₂tḗr (RV 10.39.12, Od. 4.227, both checked; Lith. dukrýtė supports dʰugh₂tḗr only). The verb is honestly interpolated, though the reduplicated present doesn't follow the Vedic jā́yate. Same title as dawn-001.

*déms pótis is a phrase only in Indo-Iranian (RV 1.149.1 pátir dán, Y. 45.11 də̄ṇg patōiš, both checked). The Greek is a compound of another formation (δέσποινα, Od. 14.9, checked), so the second branch is root/formation-level for 'master'. The copula is interpolated.
